episode_title: From Car Accident Survivor to Personal Injury Attorney

real_qa.q: What was Tommy Baru's car accident in 2013 and how did it lead him to personal injury law?
real_qa.r: In 2013, while leaving work from bartending at Essence Fest in New Orleans, Tommy Baru was rear-ended on the interstate by a car traveling at 100 miles per hour, which caused the vehicle to flip multiple times. He was ejected from the car, broke his neck, and split his head open. This traumatic experience, combined with his mother-in-law's guidance as an experienced paralegal in personal injury, led him to shift his career focus from his original goal of criminal law to personal injury law.

real_qa.q: How does Tommy Baru use his bartending experience to relate to personal injury clients?
real_qa.r: Baru applies his bartending skills to understand and empathize with diverse types of people, from happy clients to difficult ones, training him to relate to clients, talk them down in stressful situations, and handle challenging interactions. He maintains referrals from former bar regulars and uses his people skills and personal connections as a key part of his client acquisition strategy, still having clients recognize him from his bartending days over a decade ago.
real_qa.requete: bartender skills personal injury attorney client relations

real_qa.q: What is the financial impact of Tommy Baru's own car wreck injury in 2013?
real_qa.r: Tommy Baru sustained a quarter of a million dollar injury but had minimal insurance policies, which taught him from the beginning how to stack policies from liability to UM coverage and navigate the claims process. Even with a better understanding than most as a law student, he was lowballed and given the runaround by adjusters, demonstrating how insurance companies undervalue legitimate injury claims.
real_qa.requete: quarter million dollar injury insurance policies

real_qa.q: What is Tommy Baru's approach to hiring and scaling his law firm?
real_qa.r: Baru prefers to keep his team small, currently employing a paralegal and office manager (a former adjuster with paralegal experience) plus an assistant. He deliberately avoids scaling to multiple attorneys because he wants to maintain quality customer service and avoid becoming the "machine" that large firms represent. He is hesitant to hire associates unless they demonstrate unique thought processes, bring their own cases and client load, and share his entrepreneurial ambition rather than simply seeking salary and benefits.
real_qa.requete: law firm scaling team hiring strategy small office

real_qa.q: Why does Tommy Baru emphasize putting personal back into personal injury law?
real_qa.r: Baru differentiates himself from billboard attorneys and TV personal injury lawyers by emphasizing his personal experience with catastrophic injury and his genuine desire to help clients recover and battle insurance companies. He believes his lived experience of being ejected from a vehicle, breaking his neck, and dealing with insurance lowballing gives him authentic empathy and credibility that most personal injury attorneys—especially those who have never been seriously injured—cannot replicate.
real_qa.requete: personal injury attorney empathy lived experience

guest.bio_context: Tommy Baru is a personal injury attorney based in Louisiana who survived a catastrophic car accident in 2013 when a vehicle rear-ended him at 100 miles per hour on the interstate, resulting in a broken neck and head injury. His mother-in-law, a paralegal with over 25 years of experience, guided him into personal injury law after his own injury experience. Prior to becoming a lawyer, Baru worked as a DJ and bartender for several years, including at Essence Fest in New Orleans, and has maintained those client relationships throughout his legal career.

real_quote: I'm trying to put personal back into personal injury because those guys you see on TV, those guys in the suits, those guys who post all over the billboards—99% of those guys have not even gotten in a car wreck, much less been catastrophically injured like I have.
